# Tobit Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_007_page_001.jpg

---

**1** They reached Ecbatana and found Raguel's house. Sarah herself came out to meet them at the door. Greetings were exchanged all around, and she brought them inside.

**2** Raguel turned to his wife Edna and said quietly, "That young man — he looks just like my cousin Tobit."

**3** "Where are you from, friends?" he asked them.

"From the tribe of Naphtali," they said. "We're among the exiles from Nineveh."

**4** "Do you know a man named Tobit? He's a kinsman of mine."

"We know him well."

"How is he? Is he in good health?"

**5** "He's alive and well."

Tobias said, "He's my father."

**6** Raguel leaped to his feet, threw his arms around Tobias, and wept. "You are the son of a fine and noble man," he said through his tears. "What a tragedy — that a man so righteous and so kind should lose his sight!"

He held his kinsman Tobias close and wept.

**7** Edna was weeping too, and so was their daughter Sarah.

**8** Raguel had a ram slaughtered and set out a proper welcome for them.

After they had cleaned up, washed, and sat down to eat, Tobias said to Raphael, "Azariah, brother — ask Raguel to give me Sarah as my wife."

**9** Raguel had caught the words and turned to Tobias: "Eat, drink, and enjoy the evening! Because the truth is — no one else has any claim to Sarah but you. I'm not legally free to give her to anyone else; you're her nearest kinsman. But I have to be honest with you, son:

**10** Seven of our men have married her. Every one of them died on his wedding night. Still — eat and drink. God will look after you."

"I won't eat or drink," Tobias said, "until this is settled."

Raguel said, "All right — she's yours, right here and now. The law of Moses says so, and heaven has decreed it. Take her as your wife and kinswoman. From this day on, you are her husband and she is your wife. She is given to you today, and for always. May the Lord of heaven bless you tonight, son, and give you his mercy and peace."

**11** Raguel called Sarah in. She came to him, and he took her by the hand and placed her hand in Tobias's hand. "She is yours," he said, "according to the law written in the book of Moses. Take her home safely to your father. God bless your journey in peace."

**12** Then he called Edna, got out a scroll, and drew up the marriage contract. They sealed it together.

**13** Only then did the meal begin.

**14** Raguel went to his wife. "Edna," he said, "get the other bedroom ready, and take her there."

**15** Edna prepared the room just as he'd asked, and she led Sarah inside. She held her daughter and wept over her, and then she dried Sarah's tears and said,

**16** "Be brave, my darling. May the Lord of heaven turn your sorrow into joy. Be brave."

Then she left her.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **v. 2 — "said quietly"**: The Greek does not specify volume, but Raguel's aside to Edna about the resemblance is a private moment of recognition. PNEUMA adds "quietly" to signal that Raguel is not speaking to the guests — a stage-direction enhancement.
- **v. 6 — "What a tragedy"**: Greek *hōs athlion* — "how wretched/miserable." PNEUMA renders this as an exclamation of genuine grief. The three-fold weeping (Raguel, Edna, Sarah) is the emotional centerpiece of the hospitality scene.
- **v. 9 — "I'm not legally free"**: PNEUMA makes the legal constraint explicit in modern idiom. The Mosaic levirate principle is the unseen force shaping this entire scene.
- **v. 10 — Tobias's refusal to eat**: This is Tobias's decisive moment of courage. After hearing about seven dead husbands, he insists on settling the marriage before touching food. PNEUMA preserves the starkness of "I won't eat or drink."
- **v. 10 — "From this day on, you are her husband"**: PNEUMA expands "you are her brother" — the marriage formula — because modern readers will not understand "brother" as a marital term without context. The meaning is preserved over the idiom.
- **v. 11 — "placed her hand in Tobias's hand"**: The Greek has Raguel giving Sarah to Tobias by the hand (*edōken autēn cheirī*). PNEUMA renders this as a tangible physical gesture — the handing of the bride.
- **vv. 15–16 — Edna's farewell**: This is one of the most poignant moments in the book. A mother sending her daughter to bed on a night when the seven previous husbands all died. PNEUMA's "Be brave, my darling" renders *tharsei, teknon* with the intimacy the moment demands. — PNEUMA
